name: irregular dual control-track pitch sequence
goal: Build a never-quite-repeating cinematic sequence by driving Osc1/Osc2 pitch from two Control Tracks with irregular lengths (e.g. 15 and 14) and independent rates (e.g. dotted quarter vs quarter), over a stable low Osc3 pulse bed.

source.title: TRAVELER Track Walkthrough by Venus Theory

prerequisites: Hybrid synth or Traveler-inspired Web Audio engine with multi-osc, stereo filter, envelopes, LFOs/mod matrix, sequenced control tracks (or automation), and FX (EQ/chorus/delay/reverb)
constraints: Original synthesis only; not affiliated with KeySolutions; do not rip Traveler samples/presets/wavetables.
Original synthesis only — design new patches from portable parameters; do not copy proprietary Traveler factory preset names, banks, wavetables, or samples.
Not affiliated with KeySolutions Sounds or Traveler; concepts mapped to generic hybrid-synth / Web Audio equivalents.
Do not rip, dump, or redistribute Traveler content.
Prefer recreating the described signal-flow and motion relationships in our browser music system or any hybrid synth with comparable modules.
Do not recreate named artist factory presets by dumping banks; invent an original sequence using the same structural idea.

steps.action: Create a stable bed on Osc3 (e.g. pulse) an octave or two below; add delay/space lightly so the bed feels cinematic but steady.
Raise Osc1 and Osc2 to much higher pitch registers; they need not sound pretty alone — they supply character over the bed.
steps.expect: High layers audible when mixed in

steps.action: Control Track A → Osc1 pitch, length 15, rate dotted-quarter (or similar). Control Track B → Osc2 pitch, length 14, rate quarter. Keep modulation depth small so pitch breaks subtly rather than jumping wildly.
steps.expect: Patterns rarely align; sequence feels alive

steps.action: Map mod wheel (or expression) to increase the depth of those pitch mods for performance tension.
Mix: keep Osc3 dominant; blend high oscs underneath. Solo high pair to verify the irregular interlocking, then restore full mix.

verification: Pattern does not trivially loop every bar
